appraisal_events.evidence: soit que M. Verdurin eût sournoisement arrangé les choses d'avance pour faire plaisir à sa femme et n'eût averti les fidèles qu'au fur et à mesure... [il] eût cherché à persuader au pianiste et au docteur Cottard que la tante de l'un et les malades de l'autre n'avaient aucun besoin d'eux... il fut obligé de leur rendre leur liberté à Constantinople.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator hints, in hedged free indirect style, that M. Verdurin may have deceptively engineered an ever-lengthening voyage and pressured the pianist and Cottard to stay against their real obligations, only to be forced to release them, casting him as controlling and ultimately overruled.

appraisal_events.evidence: il était imprudent de laisser Mme Cottard rentrer à Paris que Mme Verdurin assurait être en révolution
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin's implausible claim that Paris was 'in revolution' is presented as a transparent, manipulative pretext to keep her circle from leaving, portraying her as disingenuous.

status_effects.explanation: He is depicted as covertly manipulating and pressuring the fidèles to prolong the voyage, and as ultimately failing to keep them under his control.
Her fabricated pretext about Paris being 'in revolution' marks her as manipulative in keeping the group together.

ambiguities: The narrator hedges ('soit que... soit que...') on whether M. Verdurin deliberately engineered the extended voyage or whether it happened by chance, so the deceptiveness attributed to him is not fully endorsed as fact.
